extra.death_mask: mask = (byte_19 >> 3) & 0x1e at death. byte_19 starts as record body[27] clamped to 0x0f (cact_base_construct 0x0041a530), whose bit 3 lands on mask bit 0 and is masked off -- so only hits count: every operation-0x0e damage message of kind k > 1 ORs ((k & 0xfe) << 3) into byte_19 (cact_base_op11 0x0041a7d6; player.c's copy for the mech) and an operation-0x0b collision clears those bits again (0x0041a7eb). So mask = OR of (k & 0x1e) over the op-0x0e hits since the last collision; bit i (i = 1..4) raises group i (by_bit), several bits several ids, and no id raised falls back to group 0. Op-0x0e senders and their k: player direct fire, k = block +0x1f (Mini Gun 1, Gatling Laser 2, Electric Gun 8; 0x0045996b); sustained sweep 2 (0x0044b4ff); aimed sweep the node's +0x2b (0x0044bcaf, the Concussion Beam, block +0x1f = 4); Electric Gun link arcs 8 (0x0043d861); player arcs 8 (0x00459d8c); Shockwave strike 8 (0x0044c4eb); Riot Shield sphere 8 (sustain_sphere.c); type-88 effect links 1 (0x0042c45a); world shooters' hitscan discharge k = type-98 +0x1f, which is 0 in every row of the six maps. Rounds, missiles and blasts send no op 0x0e in the decompiled code (a blast is operation 9), so they leave the mask alone. In PA the mask is therefore 0 unless a player's direct-fire or sustained weapon hit the actor since its last collision: then 2, 4, 8 or their OR. 16 has no established sender.
extra.deaths: maps[m].deaths[role] is one entry per class byte (record body[28] = instance +0x20) the role's records carry. start_ids: what dies with mask 0 (the PA default, see death_mask), in raise order; mask.by_bit: the group id each mask bit raises instead; alternates: the group-0 coin. chain: the successors of start_ids[0] as [id, sound (table B script, see effects), delay_ticks from the previous link]; extra.chains has the chain of every id that can be raised, with how each link is reached and whether its sound goes to a player. A death with class 0 raises nothing (0x0041a2fc). Every install -- the start ids and each successor when its turn comes -- is dropped outright when no viewport's reference point is within 0x20000 world units of the effect, unless the id's flag byte has bit 0 or 2 (cact_effect_install 0x0042d0ab..0x0042d12e; extra.chains[].needs_viewer_near): a death nobody is near raises nothing, plays no sound and starts no chain.
extra.device: snd_buffer_create 0x00431f20 is always handed the RIFF's fmt and takes its standard arm: 22050 Hz, 16-bit, mono, whatever the image says (every shipped image says the same).
extra.effects: effects[bank][id] is the record cact_effect_install 0x0042d020 reads: type = body[0]; sound = record +0x16 (body[0x12]) -> instance +0x11, played via table B at a player (at_player: ids 0x3d..0x44, 0x64..0x76, 0x0042d3d6) or at the point; successor = +0x15, installed at once when +0x24 (i32 spawn countdown, raw*300>>16 ticks) is 0 and +0x32 bit 11 is clear, else when the countdown runs out. Bank 0 = GlblData's first Csfx (type-86 bank 0) plus every mission Cact effect record (csfx_records restores bank 0 after each walk); bank 1 = GlblData's second Csfx (type-86 bank 1), the player's (cact_effect_bank 0x0042bf50: actor types 1, 0x12). A later record replaces an earlier one, except that a placed record (+0x32 bit 0) never replaces a placed one (0x0042c190). Successor timing (extra fields): +0x24 == 0 and +0x32 bit 11 clear -> installed inside the parent's install, right after the parent's sound (0x0042d5dc); +0x24 != 0 -> published when the parent instance's +0x04 countdown (delay_ticks = raw*300>>16, 1/300 s; a negative one is clamped to 0 when there is a successor, 0x0042c15b) runs out (0x0042dc03), gated by the +0x18 publish counter (record +0x2c, publish_counter): a positive counter is decremented and the id published only while it stays positive, and the child inherits the decremented counter (0x0042db5d); bit 11 set (successor_at_repeat_end) -> the +0x04 countdown does not run at all (0x0042dbe0) and the successor is published when the repeat count (record +0x28 byte, repeats) runs out, one decrement per repeat period (record +0x2a, *300>>12 ticks, repeat_period_ticks) (0x0042dc99); the install also skips its immediate successor then. A raised effect id whose flag byte has bit 2 (the load-time exclusivity sweep 0x0042e1a0) and not bit 0 goes to the exclusive list instead (started only while a viewport is within 0x20000); none of the death start ids is exclusive on these maps.
extra.emitters: type-96 Prop records (cact_load_type96 0x0042fc80 -> snd_emit_build 0x0042f6c0). Listed when record +0x1d (body[0x19], `flag`) has bit 0x40: then `attached` = low byte of record +0x16 (body[0x12], `sound`), a table-A/H script id; without it the prop is silent. x, y, z are body+4/+8/+12, the same frame and units as the actors (see positions; extra.logic_x/logic_z are extracted/logic's column/row). The sound itself is placed at the model block's world point = this position plus the Cobj hit-box centre turned by the record's angles (0x0042f9c1), not applied here. 'Visible': snd_emit_draw_block 0x0042fe20 runs once per eye per frame over the 5x5 emitter cells (0x20000 world units each) around the eye's focus cell; an emitter not OFF (flag 0x10) whose quad mask overlaps the cell's drawn quarter-cell mask is drawn, and only then, with attached != 0, does snd_emit_voice_follow 0x00430100 run: a free voice slot of 32 -> snd_queue_add(attached, id | 0x40000000, x, z) and a 300-tick hold; while it keeps being drawn the hold is refreshed to 900 ticks and a spinning one's queued sound is moved. Out of view the hold runs down and the voice is released (0x0042f550).
extra.load_gate: Every SHDR but a Csac's carries a Cfun load gate (res_begin_resource 0x004168b0); zero keeps the resource out. Shipped gates: GlblData Cwav and mission type-99 records `p1_X == c || p2_X == c` over mission state words 10..15 (P1 gun/heavy/special, P2 the same; frontend/input.c FE_STATE_P1_LOADOUT), i.e. loaded iff either player carries loadout code c; four Sky Captain records on viewports (word 3) and sky_captain_level (word 19); one record on viewports == 2. These tables bypass every gate (the superset). For one loadout: drop the samples whose extra.gate fails, and resolve each cell in extra.cell_writers to its LAST writer whose weapon is loaded (writes happen in Cwav order, which gating does not reorder). Slot indices here are stable handles; retail's indices for a smaller loadout are denser but nothing observable depends on them below 128.
extra.positions: x, y, z are the raw i32 at body+4/+8/+12 = instance position[0..2] (+0x58/+0x5c/+0x60); sounds use (x, z). extracted/logic's x (column) is z/8192 here and its z (row) is x/8192.
extra.priority_limit: priority = Cshd +4 clamped 1..10 (channel allocator key priority*16+volume, snd_start 0x00433ff0); limit = +5 clamped <= 4, the per-slot polyphony cap (0x00433b30 steals the quietest when full); loop = +6, DirectSound loop flag on the whole buffer.
extra.walker: snd_loop_set_mode 0x004340c0: bit 0x20 enables, mode = code & 7; mode 0..5 loops A(34+mode) on the viewport's reserved channel; a repeat of the live mode plays B(56+mode), a change plays B(50+old mode) and stops the loop; 6 plays B61 (0x3d); 7 is silence. Both cues get their channel key lowered by 100.

_rules.lead_in: snd_sample_create 0x00431c30: with a 'smpl' chunk whose loop start (+0x34) is non-zero, the master buffer holds only frames [loop_start, loop_end] (end inclusive, clamped to the data), and the head [0, loop_start) is a sample in a slot of its own, acquired with a copy of the entry (loop byte and the four script ids cleared, so it keeps the entry's priority/limit and no script reaches it), key = a counter from 100 post-incremented on every attempt. The master slot's lead_in_slot (+0x37) names the LAST such slot of its group. A loop start of 0 hands over the whole data chunk and ignores the loop end. snd_play_lead_in 0x00434640 starts the lead-in right after the master, at the same position, through the same snd_start (no delay, kind 1) -- only from the table-A readers.
_rules.load_order: res_stream_init (0x00417350) opens GlblData and only stores the mission name; res_next_pending (0x00416470) re-opens on the mission when GlblData is exhausted; res_dispatch_chunks (0x004063c0) loads in arrival order. So: GlblData's Csfx x2, Cshd (bank 0), Cwav 1..94, then the mission's Cshd (bank 1), its Cwav, then its Cact/Csac. A Cwav is matched to the first entry (bank 0 then 1, set order, entry order) whose +2 word equals its resource id; slots are allocated densely on the first Cwav of each group (key = group & 0xff) and the entry's script ids are written into the tables only then, so a later group naming the same cell overwrites it. snd_banks_release (0x00431770) resets everything per mission.

readers.A: table_a, bound 0x47 (all 70 cells): snd_play_cued 0x00433db0 (player direct-fire weapons; three cue entries per viewport, and a cue already holding the same slot is only re-held for 0x1e rather than started again, 0x00433e34), snd_play_positioned 0x00433f00 (walker loop A34+mode, hover loops via snd_loop_set_script 0x004341d0), snd_queue_add 0x00432c20 (actor ambient body[29], prop emitters, elevator travel). These three start the slot's lead-in too.
readers.B: table_b, bound 0x45 (cell 69 unreachable): snd_play_script_channel / snd_play_script 0x00433d00 (player launch-path weapons, effect sounds at a player, stop/repeat cues B50+/B56+, UI and pickup scripts), snd_play_script_at 0x00434290 (type-98 world weapons, effect sounds at a point, elevator arrival). Never start a lead-in.
readers.H: table_h: any id 70..129 handed to either reader goes here instead (snd_script_ready_slot 0x00432c90 overrides table and bound); 130+ and 0 are refused.
readers.channel_kind: the allocator's kind: the table-A starts push 0, the table-B starts and the lead-in push 1 (0x00433d74, 0x004342b3, 0x0043465d), and kind 1 gets +100 on its key (0x00433bca), so a table-B sound outranks a table-A one of equal priority; the movement loops and music use the reserved kind 2.
readers.empty: snd_script_ready_slot answers 'none' for a slot with no registered samples.

_rules.round_robin: snd_slot_start 0x00434560: cursor = slot +0x31 (0 after snd_slots_reset); per play cursor += 1, and if cursor >= count then cursor = 0; play samples[cursor]. Samples are in Cwav arrival order, so the first play of a 4-variant slot is samples[1], then 2, 3, 0; a single sample always plays.
